state: Can is a closed Given/When/Then source language for coding agents. Its GRAMMAR.md is normative for syntax, DESIGN.md owns semantics, and the compiler has position-aware keyword completion without signatures or links. The approved UI catalog has 68 words but is not fully delivered; builtin calls have their own compiler catalog. The user asks for one authoritative help entry per supported construct: signature, meaning, example, availability and stable link. Current grammar prose and compiler delivery status have some stale discrepancies, so help must not imply that a merely approved feature works. Compare ownership choices for a pre-implementation help contract by correctness, drift risk, token-efficient agent response and maintenance cost.

help_ownership.instructions: Which ownership model should define Can construct help before a dev-server implementation plan?

criteria.compiler_registry: A versioned machine-readable compiler-owned registry gives every supported construct an ID, signature, meaning, example, availability and link; grammar and design remain normative and consistency checks compare them. Clear API and filtering, with a second maintained representation to keep aligned.
criteria.derived_sources: Annotate grammar productions, design sections and existing UI/builtin catalogs with help metadata, then generate one versioned index. This minimizes duplicate syntax ownership but requires cross-source generation and availability joins.
criteria.documentation_registry: Write one canonical Markdown help catalog with explicit stable anchors and fields; use it as the first authoring reference, then convert or generate machine data when the server is implemented. Quick to review but runtime syncing can drift.
criteria.dynamic_completion: Construct cards on demand from parser expectations and current LSP completion, linking to docs; avoid a registry. Eligibility stays local to syntax but meaning, examples and stable IDs are harder to guarantee.
